items.description: Gone: the page's one AudioContext is the webAudio of the web-audio lib, imported where it is used. Installs that lib.

items.description: Renamed to use-simulated-clock: installs it. It is a clock for a timeline that makes no sound, not one on the audio clock.

items.description: A clock for a timeline that makes no sound: it runs while playing, loops between two points, and the playhead follows it without re-rendering React. Not on the audio clock: use use-transport-clock to schedule sound

items.description: A selection rectangle for the clips of a timeline: drag across bare lane (with Shift, or in a multi-select mode) and the clips it touches join the selection

items.description: The microphone as an AnalyserNode on the shared AudioContext: raw signal, never connected to the speakers, released on stop and on unmount
items.name: use-microphone

items.description: The pitch of a signal as a live source: the note nearest the sound and its offset in cents, steadied by a median and held a moment after the sound stops, with no React render per reading
items.name: use-pitch

items.description: The live levels of a signal from its AnalyserNodes, in the shape a Meter paints from: RMS in dB per channel with a peak that holds and falls, refreshed every frame without re-rendering
items.name: use-audio-levels

items.description: Levels that move on their own, with a peak that holds and falls, in the shape a Meter paints from: a demo meter that is never at rest
items.name: use-simulated-levels

items.description: The spectrum of an AnalyserNode as a live source for Plot.Trace: dB per point on a logarithmic frequency axis, refreshed every frame without re-rendering, and its held peaks as a second source

items.description: Pink noise played through an equalizer that follows your bands, with the analyser after it: what a plot draws is what is heard

items.description: A looping pulse played through a compressor that follows your controls, with the level going in as a live source in dB: pair it with a transfer curve's Plot.Dot

items.description: A DAW-style piano roll, laid out like Sona's note editor, a scrolling roll with a playable keyboard stuck to its side, a loop brace and bar ruler stuck on top, a velocity lane stuck at the bottom and a navigator to zoom across four bars: click to add notes, drag to move or resize either edge, Alt-drag to copy, shift-click to select and move several at once, double-click a note to delete it, Fold to keep only the pitches in use, with a BPM-driven loop that plays back in real time and always-on live preview as you edit. A timeline above the grid lets you click to seek or drag out a loop range to dial in a short phrase instead of always looping the whole grid. Drop a MIDI file onto the panel (or use the Import MIDI button) to load its notes and tempo onto the grid, and Export MIDI to save the current pattern back out as a .mid file
